summary:
## Getting Started with the GoPro App (Quik)
The **GoPro app** (now called **Quik**) is a free mobile application for iOS and Android that connects to your GoPro camera via Wi-Fi. It is **optional** but provides useful features:
*   **Live Preview**: See what your camera sees to frame your shots perfectly.
*   **Full Camera Control**: Remotely adjust all settings, including resolution, frame rate, and modes.
*   **Media Management**: View, download, and share photos and videos from your camera to your phone.

## Connecting Your Camera
Connecting your camera is often the most challenging step.

### Initial Pairing Process
1.  Turn on your GoPro and enable pairing mode (usually under `Preferences > Connections > Connect Device > GoPro App`).
2.  On your phone, open the GoPro app and tap the camera icon to add a new camera.
3.  The app should find your camera. You can then name it, which is helpful if you have multiple GoPros.
4.  Accept the Bluetooth pairing request to finalize the connection.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The exact steps may vary slightly depending on your camera model. Non-touchscreen models like the Session or Fusion require using the camera's physical buttons and menus.

### Troubleshooting & Connection Tips
*   **Reconnect Easily**: After initial pairing, your camera should reconnect automatically within 8 hours. The Wi-Fi icon in the app will be blue when active. If not, turning the camera on usually reactivates the Wi-Fi.
*   **Manual Wi-Fi Selection**: If the app can't find your camera, go to your phone's Wi-Fi settings and manually select your GoPro's network. Other active Wi-Fi networks (like your home network) can cause interference.
*   **Connection Range**: The Wi-Fi connection works up to about **50 feet**, depending on the environment. Keep an eye on the signal strength indicator in the app.
*   **Limitations**:
    *   You can only connect **one camera at a time**.
    *   The Wi-Fi signal **does not travel through water**, so the connection will be lost when submerged. It should reconnect automatically once the camera is out of the water.

## Remote Control & Live View
Once connected, you can control your camera remotely.
*   **Switch Modes**: Swipe left or right on the live preview to cycle between Video, Photo, and Time-Lapse modes.
*   **Adjust Settings**: Tap the settings icon to change mode-specific settings (like resolution and frame rate) and general camera settings.
*   **Start/Stop Recording**: Tap the large circular record button to start and stop recording.

> [!TIP]
> Rotate your phone to landscape mode for a larger horizontal live preview. For vertical videos, rotating the camera vertically will show a full-frame vertical preview in the app.

### Understanding Live Preview Limitations
*   **"Preview Not Available"**: This message appears if your phone is not powerful enough to display a live feed of the selected settings (e.g., 4K at 60fps). The camera **is still recording** correctly.
*   **Trade-off**: To see a live preview, you may need to lower the recording resolution or frame rate.
*   **Preview Quality**: The live preview feed is a lower-resolution stream for framing purposes. It will appear blurrier or more pixelated than the final high-resolution footage stored on the camera's SD card.

## Managing Your Media
All photos and videos are stored on the camera's microSD card. Access them in the app via the media icon.

*   **View & Organize**: Media is organized by date.
*   **Download**: You **must download** files to your phone before editing or deleting them from the camera.
*   **Video Tools**:
    *   **Trim**: Create shorter clips for easy sharing.
    *   **Grab Photo**: Extract a high-quality still image from a video frame.
    *   **Slow Motion**: Play back high-frame-rate clips (60fps+) at half-speed.
    *   **GPS Stickers**: If GPS was enabled during recording, you can overlay data like your speed, a map, or G-force.
*   **High-Resolution Files**: Even if you can't preview a high-res video in the app, you can still download it. The app will convert it to a compatible format for viewing on your phone if necessary.

## Key App Features
*   **QuikStories**: For Hero 5 and newer, the app can automatically download recent footage and create a short, edited video for you. This is a temporary process and requires significant free storage on your phone.
*   **Wireless Firmware Updates**: The app will notify you when a new firmware update is available. It downloads the update to your phone and transfers it to your camera, ensuring you have the latest features and bug fixes. You can verify the installed version under `Camera Info`.
transcription:
## Introduction to the GoPro App (Quik)

Hi my name is Jordan Hetrick. I'm the author of books about how to use your GoPro cameras and I've had a lot of requests to the create a tutorial showing the ins and outs of the GoPro app. So I'm gonna do my best to answer any questions I've had over the years relating to the GoPro App and also give you some helpful tips to navigate through it.

First of all, the GoPro App is GoPro's mobile app which allows you to use your camera's Wi-Fi connection to connect to your phone or tablet. You can then use the GoPro app to adjust all of your camera settings. You can also see a live preview of the composition, which is really useful as well as transfer media and also do a few other functions.

The GoPro App is optional. You can use your GoPro to its full potential even if you choose not to use the GoPro app, but the app does provide some useful tools for composing shots and definitely adds some vital options when you want to transfer media. The GoPro app is free and available for iOS through the App Store or for Android through Google Play.

Alright, let's check out the GoPro app.

## Initial Camera Pairing & Connection

The first step of course is just to connect your camera to the GoPro app. Connecting the camera to the app is definitely the step where people have had the most trouble. Once you've updated the firmware, it should be easier to connect back to the app but it can be a little tricky to connect the first time if you haven't updated that firmware. Here's how it's supposed to connect the first time that you pair your camera to the app.

Just turn your camera on and swipe down from the top of the screen. Tap on preferences and then tap on connections. Tap connect device and select the GoPro app and that's going to put your camera into pairing mode. This process may be slightly different depending on your camera model, but it should be very similar for all of the newer cameras. If you're using the Session or the Fusion, you're gonna have to use the menus since there's no touch screen on those cameras.

Once your camera's on in pairing mode, open the app, tap the camera icon, and then select add camera. The app should say that it's found your camera and that it's connected. That will give you the option to change the camera name, which is pretty helpful especially if you're using multiple GoPro cameras. Then it's gonna say your camera's ready but it'll probably ask you to pair using Bluetooth, so you can just tap pair and then your camera should be connected. You should be able to see a live view through your camera's lens.

## Maintaining & Troubleshooting Your Connection

Once you've set up that initial connection you should be able to go back into the GoPro app within the next eight hours and see your camera, and this Wi-Fi icon here should be blue. That means your Wi-Fi signal is still active and able to connect to the GoPro app. If that icon there is not blue, usually you can turn your camera on and that will reactivate the Wi-Fi and you'll be able to connect to the GoPro app again. So that's how it's supposed to work, ideally.

If your phone or tablet doesn't see your camera's Wi-Fi signal, the GoPro app's gonna tell you it can't find the camera. You may need to go into your Wi-Fi settings and select your device. Sometimes if you have a home Wi-Fi network or other Wi-Fi network it might be selected and interfere with the camera's Wi-Fi network. And once you get your camera connected there under the Wi-Fi settings, you can go back into the app and you should see this blue icon is highlighted here. That means your camera's Wi-Fi signal is on and connected to the phone or tablet.

The connection distance between your camera and the phone or tablet really depends on your camera model and also on the environment around you. You should be able to get up to about 50 feet away and still maintain that connection. You can try to keep an eye on the Wi-Fi signal here, and if you keep it at 2 bars you're gonna have the best connection to the GoPro app. You can only connect one camera to the app at a time. You can't connect multiple cameras, but you can save multiple cameras within the app so you can switch between those cameras. Also, once your camera goes underwater, you'll lose that connection to the GoPro app because the Wi-Fi signal can't travel through water, but once it comes back up above the water it should be able to reconnect.

## Live View: Changing Modes & Settings

Now that you're connected to the app, I want to show you how to use the app while you're filming to change your settings and also adjust your composition. So once your camera is connected, you can just tap the camera icon here and that'll show you a live view through a camera's viewfinder. You can swipe left or right and that'll change between the different modes on your camera, which will vary depending on your camera model. If you're on the Hero 7 Black, this is for live streaming. I won't go into live streaming right now but it's a very cool feature you can use for social media. It's only available on the Hero 7 black though.

As you swipe between the different modes this will show you the settings for that mode. If you tap on the capture icon here, that'll give you the options to change capture modes within a new mode. So for a video, there's video and looping. If you're in time-lapse, for example, it's going to show you the options for time-lapse mode which will vary slightly depending on your camera model. Once you've selected the mode you want to use, you can press the settings icon here and that allows you to change all the settings for the mode that you're in.

So all of the settings at the top and remote settings are for that current mode. Because we're in video mode, you'll see the video settings here, and down below are some of the general settings for your camera that you can change when any mode is selected. So under video for example, change the resolution, frame rate, etc. Once you've selected the settings you want to use, you can tap Done and you'll go back into the live view through the camera's lens. Then you can tap the circle icon here and that'll allow you to start recording through your camera.

## Understanding Live Preview Limitations

When you start recording if you see a 'preview not available' like this, that just means that your phone's not compatible with the setting that you're using on your GoPro. The video will still record and as long as you don't need to see it, you can keep recording at that resolution. If you really want to be able to see a live preview through your phone while you're filming, you'll have to lower the resolution or the frames per second until you get to one that's compatible with your phone settings. For example on this phone, if I step it down to 4k at 30 frames per second then I can see that live preview as I'm filming. The trade-off of course is that you're gonna have to film at a lower resolution so you can see that live preview. And if you plan to edit your videos on a computer where you can actually utilize that full resolution, I recommend skipping out on the live preview as it's filming and just film at the highest resolution possible.

But it really depends what your end goal is for the video. If you start recording a video and then you close the app, your camera is still going to continue recording, so it's just good to know that your camera is not reliant on the app to record a video. If you do disconnect, you can also reconnect to the app while a video's recording or while the time lapse is recording. If you're recording horizontally for landscape shots, then you can rotate your phone and you'll actually see a larger view of what you're recording through the GoPro app. Or if you choose to rotate your GoPro camera vertically for portrait shots, you can actually see the full frame in the GoPro app with your phone held vertically like this. It's also important to know that as you record your videos, the actual preview on your phone using the GoPro app is not the same resolution that's going to be recorded on your GoPro camera. It's more conceptual and it's just so you can have that live view using the GoPro app. So don't be disappointed if it looks a little blurry or pixelated as you're recording the shots because once you download the footage it won't look like that.

## Viewing & Managing Your Media

When you record photos and videos, they're stored on your camera's micro SD card. If you're already in your camera's live view, you can just tap this media icon here and you can view your media. You can also go directly to your media from the camera's home screen by tapping this icon. This icon over here is to auto upload your footage to the cloud if you're using GoPro Plus.

So when you open up your media the videos and photos are all organized by date, so you can scroll through to find a video or photo you want to view. When you tap on a photo or video there will be some options down here at the bottom of the screen. These options will vary depending on which type of media you're looking at. So if you tap on a photo for example, you'll see these three icons at the bottom. This first one here is share. If you tap on that share icon you can share that photo directly to Instagram or Facebook or Twitter or download it to your phone. This icon here in the middle is the info icon which isn't that necessary usually for photos, but as you get into video it can be more important. And this here of course is the download icon so you can download the photo and save it to your phone. All of the recorded videos and photos are stored on your camera's micro SD card so you want to make sure you save them to your phone or tablet to edit them and especially before deleting them.

If you select a video, these will be the icons that you see down here at the bottom. You can push play on the video and on the right side of the play button you'll see there's a slow motion icon if you recorded your video at 60 frames per second or higher. And right now on the GoPro app it's only got regular speed and half speed. So even though I recorded this clip at 240 frames per second, it still only plays it at half speed, so you can edit it to a slower motion than it's actually going to show here in the GoPro app. This scissors icon down here is the trim icon that just allows you to trim your video clips to a shorter clip, which is useful for sharing to social media or if you just want to edit out parts of the video. The second icon here is to grab a photo from your video. So if you tap that, you can actually scroll through the video to find the exact frame that you want to extract and save it as a photo. This icon here is the share icon, which is the same as if you were looking at a photo. The info icon here is a little more useful with video because you can see your frame rate and resolution. This is the download icon again and that's just to save the videos to your phone. And this icon here is the stickers icon. If you recorded your video using GPS, you can add stickers to your video such as maps and g-force, etc. If you decide you don't want those on your video you can just tap on them and drag them down to the trashcan here. If you recorded a video at a really high resolution, say at 4k 60 frames per second for example, you might not be able to view the video directly using the GoPro app, but you can save the video to your phone and the GoPro app will convert it if it needs to to a resolution that's compatible with your phone, and then you can view it that way.

## Auto-Editing with QuikStories

If you're using a Hero 5 or newer camera, another one of the cool features of the GoPro app is using QuikStories. When you open up the GoPro app it'll see that your camera's got recent footage on it and it'll prompt you to download it. If you download it, it'll save temporary files to your phone and auto-edit a quick story for you. I'm not gonna go into editing the quick stories right now because that's using the Quik app and that could be a whole another video. You do have to have a lot of storage on your phone because it's going to be downloading all of the recent footage and using that to create your quick stories, but those are temporary files. So as long as you have some open storage on your phone those files will be deleted later if you choose not to save them to your phone.

## Updating Camera Firmware Wirelessly

Another useful feature of the GoPro app is that you can update your camera's firmware wirelessly. As soon as the new firmware is released for your camera's model, the GoPro app will prompt you to download the update. The update will download on your phone using Wi-Fi, or if you go into the settings for the GoPro app, you can also allow it to download using your data. It'll then transfer it to your camera and update the firmware. By updating your firmware, you can ensure that you've got the most up-to-date features for your camera model as well as correct any problems from previous releases. If you want to check to make sure that the current version was installed, you can just check here on the settings and look at your camera info version and it should show the most recent release that you just downloaded.

## Conclusion & Outro

I really hope you enjoyed the tutorial. Please buy a copy of my book. It would really help me out, and I know it would help you out too. Thanks so much for all the support and the inspiration, and I really hope that I inspired you as well. If you like this video, please give it a like and also subscribe to my channel to stay tuned for more tutorials in the future. Thanks again and have fun GoPro-ing.
